run.question:
Alertmanager alert PendingPodsDetected (severity critical) is firing for service otel-demo/otel-demo since 2026-11-18T01:50:10Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The PendingPodsDetected alert for otel-demo is explained by two unschedulable pods, ad-dd7f45975-mw86p and cart-5b597c6db5-pkzkh, both carrying spec.nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=invalid-node. The 5-node cluster has no node with hostname invalid-node, and the scheduler reported for both pods '0/5 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: }, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector'. The setting lives in the pod templates of Deployments otel-demo/ad and otel-demo/cart (deployment revision 2, Helm release otel-demo); those are the only 2 workloads cluster-wide with this bogus nodeSelector. New ReplicaSets ad-dd7f45975 and cart-5b597c6db5 were created at 01:49:13Z and 01:49:21Z by a rollout that scaled them from 0 to 1, producing the pending pods ~1 minute before the alert started at 01:50:10Z. The previous ReplicaSets (ad-554b849958, cart-755465879b) still run one ready pod each with the same image tag and no nodeSelector, and the ad/cart Endpoints each still have one ready address, so no service outage was observed; the rollout is simply stuck (each Deployment shows replicas 2, readyReplicas 1, unavailableReplicas 1, Progressing). Small pre-existing error-span counts on ad (flagd EventStream spans started at 01:07:39Z and 01:17:42Z with rpc.grpc.status_code 4) predate the pod change and are not tied to this alert. Who or what set the invalid nodeSelector cannot be verified: change history is not integrated and mutating webhook configuration could not be read, so the conclusion is partial with the fault-application mechanism unresolved.

claims.text: Exactly two pods were Pending cluster-wide, both in namespace otel-demo: ad-dd7f45975-mw86p (created 01:49:13Z) and cart-5b597c6db5-pkzkh (created 01:49:21Z); each has PodScheduled=False with reason Unschedulable.

For both pending pods the scheduler event message is exactly: '0/5 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: }, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/5 nodes are available: 5 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' FailedScheduling events ran from 01:49:13Z/01:49:21Z through 01:59:36Z with count 3 each.
The two pending pods carry spec.nodeSelector {"kubernetes.io/hostname":"invalid-node"}; the pod-level nodeSelector is the only placement constraint (affinity is null).

The cluster has 5 nodes with kubernetes.io/hostname values i-01a47734339426210 (control-plane, NoSchedule taint), i-037e40963128cbd9f, i-0424ef08cd107882f, i-08831c4b8af18ed15 and i-097278082719f10ba; none of them has hostname 'invalid-node'.

Deployments otel-demo/ad and otel-demo/cart have spec.template.spec.nodeSelector {"kubernetes.io/hostname":"invalid-node"} and deployment.kubernetes.io/revision 2; they are the only 2 of the 21 otel-demo Deployments, and the only 2 of 36 Deployments cluster-wide, whose pod template sets nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname to invalid-node (other workloads use kubernetes.io/os: linux or no nodeSelector).

ReplicaSet ad-dd7f45975 (created 01:49:13Z) and cart-5b597c6db5 (created 01:49:21Z) carry the invalid-node nodeSelector, while the older ReplicaSets ad-554b849958 (01:11:48Z) and cart-755465879b (01:11:47Z) have no nodeSelector and 1 ready replica each; the container image reference ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad / 2.1.3-cart is identical between old and new ReplicaSets.

Normal events show Deployment ad scaled ReplicaSet ad-dd7f45975 from 0 to 1 at 01:49:13Z and Deployment cart scaled ReplicaSet cart-5b597c6db5 from 0 to 1 at 01:49:21Z, each followed by ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate 'Created pod: ...' — i.e. a rollout created the pending pods about one minute before the alert start 01:50:10Z.

Deployment otel-demo/ad status is replicas 2, readyReplicas 1, availableReplicas 1, unavailableReplicas 1 with Progressing condition (message 'ReplicaSet "ad-dd7f45975" is progressing'), and Deployment otel-demo/cart status is replicas 2, readyReplicas 1, availableReplicas 1, unavailableReplicas 1 with Progressing condition (message 'ReplicaSet "cart-5b597c6db5" is progressing').

Endpoints for Service ad and Service cart each still expose exactly one ready address, pointing at the older pods ad-554b849958-42mdm (100.96.3.180) and cart-755465879b-bgb2p (100.96.3.205) on node i-037e40963128cbd9f.

The older pods ad-554b849958-42mdm (imageID ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo@sha256:c9d4f94314937eb3b61cf8b1672b7e87fab95442bd1d01f8d32f43a882255944) and cart-755465879b-bgb2p (sha256:84ce75e56697c94a8ab00258b68babc06c042ae6f1e98c061f52f0c748d0cdd5) are Running with 0 restarts and are owned by those older ReplicaSets; the two pending pods have no container statuses and no imageID (nothing was pulled).

In the 01:04:56Z–02:04:56Z metric window ad had STATUS_CODE_ERROR span increase ≈3.05 and cart had no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series (only STATUS_CODE_UNSET ≈38901.7); ad's error spans are operation flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream started 01:07:39Z and 01:17:42Z with rpc.grpc.status_code 4 and ~600 s duration, whereas the pending pods were created at 01:49:13Z/01:49:21Z, so those errors predate the rollout.

The invalid nodeSelector was written into the pod templates of Deployments otel-demo/ad and otel-demo/cart by a configuration change to the Helm release otel-demo (deployment revision 2), which created ReplicaSets ad-dd7f45975 and cart-5b597c6db5 and left one unschedulable surge pod per Deployment; the change's author and exact application timestamp are not observable in this Run.

Rejected: the control-plane NoSchedule taint alone explains the pending pods. The scheduler message combines 1 tainted node with 4 nodes that 'didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector', and the pods' nodeSelector names hostname invalid-node, which no node in the cluster has, so the selector is the binding constraint for the 4 worker nodes.

Rejected: the alert reflects an ad or cart application failure. The alert counts pending pods, only two pods are Pending cluster-wide, ad's small error-span count comes from long-lived flagd EventStream spans that started before the rollout, and cart had no error-status spans in the window.

Not all workloads are affected: of 23 pods in otel-demo, 21 are Running and Ready (e.g. accounting-58d4b6c958-h9bsj, checkout-5dccddf8bb-dt94w, payment-55766d76b9-66qmg), and ad/cart Service endpoints still resolve to running backends, so the observed impact is limited to the two pending pods and the two stalled rollouts.

No ConfigMap object in the cluster (55 processed, .data compared as text) contains the string 'invalid-node', and no CustomResourceDefinition (28 processed) matches chaos/litmus/fault/inject, so no fault-injection CRD was found; the string appears in the Deployment and ReplicaSet specs, which could not be traced back to a stored configuration object.

gaps: No change-history integration is available, so who or what set kubernetes.io/hostname=invalid-node on Deployments otel-demo/ad and otel-demo/cart, and the exact moment of the edit (as opposed to the rollout at 01:49:13Z/01:49:21Z), cannot be verified.

mutatingwebhookconfigurations queries failed twice with SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so an admission webhook or controller injecting the nodeSelector cannot be excluded as the source; the cronjobs query also failed with SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE.

Prometheus returned no kube_* metric names ({__name__=~"kube_.*"} returned nothing) and no kube_deployment_status_replicas_available series for otel-demo, so kube-state-metrics views of pod phase and deployment replica history (e.g. how long the two pods were Pending before 02:04:59Z) are unknown; the pending count relies on the API snapshot and events.
The PendingPodsDetected alerting rule was not returned by list_prometheus_rules (no rule named PendingPodsDetected), so the alert expression and its exact evaluation times were not verified.

Application-log error scans of ad-554b849958-42mdm and cart-755465879b-bgb2p for 01:30:00Z-02:04:56Z returned no_data (no matching lines among 3418 and 11089 lines read), so the application-level health of ad and cart is not established from logs.
No Application-level failure attributable to the pending pods was observed; whether ad/cart would degrade if the old pods were replaced (which would leave zero schedulable replicas) was not tested.

Events in namespace data-recorders (2 Pod FailedScheduling, plus PVC WaitForFirstConsumer/Provisioning activity) were outside this alert's namespace and were not investigated; those pods were not Pending at query time.
next_steps: Review the Helm release otel-demo history/values (via a change-history source) to find the change that set nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname: invalid-node on Deployments ad and cart, and confirm the intended value.

Advisory: remove or correct spec.template.spec.nodeSelector {"kubernetes.io/hostname":"invalid-node"} on Deployments otel-demo/ad and otel-demo/cart so the surge pods can schedule; until then the old pods remain the only backends and a replacement of those pods would leave each service with no schedulable replica.

Advisory: restore scraping of kube-state-metrics (kube_pod_status_phase, kube_deployment_status_replicas_*) so pending-pod alerts are backed by metric history, and verify the PendingPodsDetected rule is loaded/source-visible.
Advisory: confirm no mutating admission webhook or controller is injecting hostname nodeSelectors once mutatingwebhookconfigurations can be read.
